{{Wireless adapter |brand=Nikon |model=WU-1a |revision= |upc= |ean= |asin= |price= |est_release_date= |fcc_date=04/18/2012 |manuf_country=Japan |is_manuf=No |manuf= |manuf_model= |manuf_rev= |availability= |if=not actually a wireless adapter |if_bus_version= |if_connector_type= |form_factor= |vendor_id= |device_id= |subvendor_id= |subdevice_id= |id_string= |fcc_id=CGJ2148EA |ic_id= |chip1_brand=Broadcom |chip1_model=BCM43362 |chip2_brand= |chip2_model= |chip3_brand= |chip3_model= |chip4_brand= |chip4_model= |addl_chips= |accessible_UART=No |flags= |ant_conn= |802dot11_protocols=bgn |txchains=1 |rxchains=1 |sstreams=1 |oui= |lin_driver= |win_driver= }} This device serves as a portable access point for the '''Nikon''' D3200 camera allowing pictures to be taken remotely with an Android phone.
[http://hackaday.com/2012/11/10/nikon-wu-1a-wifi-dongle-hacking/ Nikon WU-1a WiFi dongle hacking on '''Hack a Day'''] :[https://docs.google.com/presentation/pub?id=1Yi2uh3s12IFe024xsMrO-jwut-NEjDoaIl8DzmaRE_g#slide=id.g3a08561d_1_27 Hacking the Nikon WU-1a] (slides) ::"F205RG6", "8NME5VG", and "SGR201Y" appears to be on the '''STM''' microcontroller. ::BCM43362KUBG is on the '''Broadcom''' wireless chip. This is a BCM43362.
This device contains a '''STMicroelectronics''' microcontroller (STM32F205), a '''STMicroelectronics''' USB OTG transciever, and a '''Broadcom''' wireless chip (BCM43362).
Internal / external pictures, lsusb output: [https://nikonhacker.com/wiki/WU-1a]
